model.method: PatchCore (in-repo), k=1, 3x3 pooling, Gaussian sigma 4, whole image resized to 224 x 224

assumptions: Costs are relative. A false reject costs 1 and an escaped defect costs r = 20; defects are assumed to be p = 2% of items. Both are assumptions, not plant figures; the sensitivity grid covers r = 5 to 100 and p = 0.5% to 5%.

Rates are per class (share of normals rejected, share of defects passed) and are weighted by p, so the threshold does not depend on VisA's test mix (two thirds anomalous). Cost per 1000 items is the weighted cost times 1000.
Validation and test are 50/50 halves of the official test split, so each half holds only 25 to 50 normal and 50 anomalous images: intervals are wide and thresholds are noisy.
Images are VisA product photos, not images from the plant; their link to a line is simulated elsewhere in this project and labelled.
The review band assumes a reviewer decides every image in it correctly and ignores review effort. Its width is set on validation so that 10% of items, weighted by p, are routed to review.
Pixel metrics are computed on the 224 x 224 maps and masks, not at the original resolution.

primary.source: Zou et al., SPot-the-Difference self-supervised pre-training for anomaly detection and segmentation (the VisA paper)
primary.table: Table 6, '1-class performance evaluation on VisA and MVTec-AD with PatchCore', backbone Wide ResNet50, row 'Sup. pre-train', VisA columns
primary.scope: average over VisA's 12 classes, one model per class; the table does not state the input resolution or AUPRO

secondary.source: SoftPatch+ (Fully unsupervised anomaly detection with noisy data)
secondary.table: Table 3 (image AUROC) and Table 4 (pixel AUROC), 'upperbound' column of the 'No Overlap' setting, which is PatchCore trained on clean normal images, Wide-ResNet50, 10% coreset
secondary.caveat: The test set is that paper's 8%-noise protocol variant, not necessarily the official 1cls test split, and its VisA input resolution is not stated (it states 256 resize with 224 centre crop for MVTec AD only).

published.setup_note: Ours: wide_resnet50_2 IMAGENET1K_V1, whole image resized to 224 x 224 without cropping, layers 2 and 3, coreset up to 10% or 16,384 patches, one model per subset, official 1cls train. Backbone and one-class protocol match the primary source, whose figures are averages over 12 classes while ours are averages over the six food subsets, so the two averages cover different sets of classes. No source found reports PatchCore AUPRO per class on VisA.

first_run.note: First run used a resize to 256 and a centre crop to 224, which cut the defect entirely out of the image for 18 of 100 macaroni2 anomalies (24 had under half inside). The preprocessing now resizes the whole image to 224 x 224 and the models were refitted. Image AUROC did not improve on the macaroni subsets (macaroni1 and macaroni2 are lower); this was not investigated further, and squeezing a wide image into a square, which makes small defects smaller, is one possible factor.
first_run.columns: image AUROC, pixel AUROC, pixel AUPRO
